session.title: DASA 2027 route, university shortlist and JEE Main plan
session.participants: Darsh, his mother, Kalil (EduAakashaA mentor), Dr. Saravanan Veerasamy (mentor)
session.agenda:
1. JEE Main application status
2. NTU, NUS and HKU: dates, costs, scholarships, deposits
3. Study in India (SII) quota as a backup
4. Which universities to keep
5. IIT Delhi Abu Dhabi (CAET)
6. JEE Main preparation plan around school exams
7. Meeting rhythm and next steps
session.shared_summary:
DECISIONS
- JEE Main Session 1 application is done.
- Foreign universities: keep it to one or two. NTU Singapore is the first choice (better chance given the competition, good feedback from students the mentors know). NUS is the optional second. HKU is put on hold for now: its fee is about double NUS and the family does not want many options. Its first round closes 25 Nov 2026, so nothing needs to be submitted unless the family changes its mind.
- Do not pay application or offer deposits at several universities. Offer deposits are non-refundable and results are only known after the boards.
- Study in India (SII) quota is a backup: register on the portal and look at the participating colleges (many NITs and some private colleges).
- IIT Delhi Abu Dhabi (CAET): the family plans to apply for the January and April sessions. Registration for January opens in December.

WHAT WAS EXPLAINED
- Scholarships at all three universities are applied for after an offer, not before. They depend on the programme, marks and achievements. CBSE school projects do not count; international certifications and awards can (HKU gives bonus points; NTU looks at marks).
- Offers are based on predicted marks first and confirmed on the board results. After an offer there is a date to pay the deposit and accept, or the offer is withdrawn. HKU offers can start in December. The accept-by period at NTU and NUS is not confirmed yet (guess: about 10 days to 2 weeks), so we will ask the universities.
- Interviews are online and only some applicants are called. Being called is not a sign of admission.
- Study in India (SII): each college sends its own link after the JEE result; if few apply the criteria are relaxed (some colleges take 65 to 70 percent), if many apply JEE counts.

JEE MAIN PLAN (about 1 to 1.5 months left)
- Order in the exam: Chemistry first, then Physics, Maths last and only the quick ones.
- Targets: about 15 of 25 correct in Chemistry, about 10 of 25 in Physics, 3 to 5 in Maths. 30 correct out of 75 is enough for the target range. Do not touch a question you are not sure of: one mark can be several hundred ranks.
- Maths: no fixed block; do it when tired or bored. Spend most time on Chemistry, then Physics topics already known.
- Darsh ticks the topics he is 100 percent confident in; the mentors build a 30 to 40 day schedule and a daily routine from past-year weightage.

SCHOOL CALENDAR (as told by Darsh)
- Model exams 25 Nov to 16 Dec (portion-based). Vacation from 16 Dec to about 1 to 4 Jan: full-time JEE preparation.
- Practical exams about 10 to 20 Jan. Two pre-boards fall after 20 Jan; the school will let him skip one that clashes with JEE Main (marks above 40 percent are enough).
- Classes are only about three a week now.

MEETINGS: a 30-minute check-in every week or every two weeks was agreed in principle.
session.mentor_notes:
Private notes.
- Darsh's school paper tests (out of 300): 80 to 120, class highest 200. Chemistry is his best (20 questions attempted easily); Maths and Physics term 1 are weak (7 to 8 Maths questions attempted; Maths 30 to 40 marks when basics hold). Negative marks of minus 10 to 11 per paper: the main thing to fix.
- Dr. Saravanan's advice was to keep one, at most two, foreign universities; he only has first-hand knowledge of Singapore (NTU), none of Hong Kong. The HKU decision is therefore the family's, not a recommendation from data. Re-open it only if HKU's fee and the first-round date still look right to them.
- He suggested trying the SII portal with a placeholder name to see the college list. For any real application the family must use true details; the nationality drop-down had no India option and Dr. Saravanan suggested UAE: confirm the correct choice with the SII helpdesk before a real registration.
- Roadmap NTU line says 93 percent minimum; the parents' guide slide said 90 percent. Check on NTU's India Standard 12 page before telling the family.
- The family asked about deposits at several universities and about the Study in India fair in Dubai. The fair is an education fair, not the SII quota.
- Darsh asked for help planning his schedule: he feels things are getting scattered. Keep the plan short and printable.
- Darsh was not yet in the mentor WhatsApp group; added during the call.
